title: Image-to-Image Translation with Conditional Adversarial Networks
layout_note: Two cases separated by a vertical dotted rule: on the left, edge sketch x -> generator G -> synthesized photo G(x), which is bracketed together with a copy of x (reached by a dashed curved arrow) and fed to discriminator D, ending in a red 'fake'; on the right, a real photo y bracketed with its edge sketch x into the same D, ending in a green 'real'.
grouping: No boxes or panels; the two training cases are split only by a dotted vertical rule, and each {sketch, photo} pair is grouped by a square bracket that closes into the arrow entering D.
shapes_depth: Minimal flat glyphs: each network (G, D) is three narrow white upright rectangles with black outlines, labelled by a single italic letter above; data are the actual images (edge sketches and shoe photos) with italic math labels x, y, G(x).
proposed_highlight: The conditioning - the paper's point - is drawn as the input sketch x being bracketed with the photo in both cases (copied to D by a dashed curved arrow on the fake side); the verdicts are the only colour, a red 'fake' and a green 'real'.
lesson: Show a conditional discriminator as two mirrored cases split by a dotted rule, each bracketing the condition with the image into the same three-bar D glyph, and colour only the outputs (red fake, green real).
notes: year = arXiv preprint year; no venue printed on the arXiv first page; remembered venue CVPR 2017 (not verified). The figure is small and draws only the adversarial part; the L1 term and the U-Net generator are in Figure 3.

arrangement.units: two unframed halves split by a vertical dotted rule: the fake pair path (with G) on the left, the real pair path on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: real image thumbnails: an edge sketch x on the left of each half and a real shoe photo y on the right half
arrangement.losses_at: no loss box; the discriminator's verdict words 'fake' (red) and 'real' (green) at the right end of each half stand for the objective
arrangement.shared: D is drawn twice as the same three-bar glyph with the same label, one per half; x is drawn twice on the fake side (input and copy to D)

core.what: two mirrored halves behind a dotted rule: the generated pair (x, G(x)) into D giving 'fake' on the left and the real pair (x, y) into the same D giving 'real' on the right

relations.form: left half and right half each end in an identical D three-bar glyph followed by a verdict word, split by a vertical dotted rule
in each half two images stacked vertically are joined by a bracket into D: G(x) over x on the left, y over x on the right, so the discriminator always sees the edge map with an output
left half reads left to right: edge sketch x, generator G (three bars), synthesized shoe G(x)
a dashed curved arrow copies x from the input down to the lower slot of the fake pair, the same x that conditions the real pair

channels.colour: colour only on the verdicts: red 'fake' and green 'real'; images are the data in their own colours
channels.shape: three vertical bars = a network (G or D); images = data; bracket = a pair fed together
channels.line: solid = network data flow, dashed curve = copying the condition x into the pair; dotted vertical rule = separates the two cases

quality.strengths: The conditional-GAN idea is shown by position: both halves pair the same edge map with an output and feed identical D glyphs, so the only difference between fake and real is the upper image; all data are actual images, networks are reduced to small glyphs, and lines are short and straight.
quality.weaknesses: The dashed copy of x curves under G and could be misread as a second path through the network; the generator's U-Net and the L1 loss are not drawn, so only the adversarial half of the objective appears.

insights.structure: Two mirrored cases sit side by side behind a dotted rule - generated pair on the left with G in front, real pair on the right - and both end in an identical D glyph.
insights.data: Inputs and outputs are the actual images (edge sketches, synthesized and real shoe photos) labelled with italic x, y, G(x); networks shrink to three outlined bars.
insights.emphasis: The only colour is the verdict text, red 'fake' and green 'real', and the conditional input is made visible by bracketing x with each photo going into D.
insights.flow: Each half reads left to right along straight black arrows; a dashed curved arrow carries x from the input down to D's bracket on the fake side.
insights.avoid: The three-bar network glyphs carry no information about the architecture, and the generator's training signal (L1 term) is not drawn at all, so the figure explains only half of the objective.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
